messages:
Sam Patel: Getting intermittent 502s in the Console when creating a dedicated deployment. UI shows spinner then "Something went wrong". I captured one network row with header x-request-id: req_deploy_9c3a at 2026-03-16T21:05:12Z. Can someone post exact steps for HAR + console capture and a curl repro pattern? URL: https://app.redwood.ai/deploy
Alex Gomez: Sorry about that, we can help. Please include: a full HAR (with content), the Console logs (Console tab), the failing request row (method/path/status), and the full x-request-id header value. Also include account email/org and local time zone. Below are step-by-step instructions for major browsers + a curl template.
Alex Gomez: Chrome / Edge (instructions):
1) Open DevTools (F12 or Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+I)
2) Network tab -> check "Preserve log" and enable "Disable cache" if you can
3) Keep Console tab open to capture errors
4) Reproduce the failure
5) Right-click any row -> "Save all as HAR with content" (or "Export HAR")
6) Console -> right-click -> "Save as..." to export logs, or copy the console output to a .log file
7) If you only want one request, right-click the failing row -> Copy -> "Copy as cURL (bash)" and include that in your reply
8) Redact long secrets (replace Authorization values with <redacted>) but DO NOT alter x-request-id
Morgan Lee: Example curl you can edit and paste back (swap path/host with exact values from your HAR):
```
curl 'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/deployments' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer <redacted>' \
  -H 'x-request-id: req_deploy_9c3a' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  --data-raw '{"name":"staging-test","model":"redwood-7b"}' \
  -v
```
Morgan Lee: If you can't share the full HAR, at minimum send: method, path, status code, response body, and the exact x-request-id value.
Priya Shah: Firefox steps:
1) Web Developer -> Network -> check "Persist logs"
2) Reproduce the issue
3) Click the gear in Network pane -> "Save all as HAR"
Safari (macOS):
1) Safari Preferences -> Advanced -> check "Show Develop menu"
2) Develop -> Show Web Inspector -> Network -> reproduce -> right click -> Export HAR
Priya Shah: Helpful tips:
- Try an incognito/private window to reduce extension noise
- If HAR contains sensitive tokens, open it in a text editor and replace long token strings with <redacted> (leave x-request-id untouched)
- If the x-request-id is missing (some proxies rename it), also check for headers like request-id or x-rw-req-id in the request/response headers
Alex Gomez: Upload guidance:
- Use support upload: https://support.redwood.ai/upload (select "Debug bundle")
- Put the HAR, Console log, and a small README.txt with repro steps, account email, and timestamp in a zip if possible
- Max single file before compression: 200MB. If larger, share a link and paste it here.
support-bot: Note: label your upload filename or notes with the root request id (req_deploy_9c3a) to speed routing. Accepted file types: .har, .log, .zip, .tar.gz
Sam Patel: Thanks — uploading now. I'm on macOS 13.5, Chrome 114.0.5735.133, local timezone PST. Uploaded debug_bundle_deploy_1719760200.zip to support with notes and included the cURL and console log. Link: https://support.redwood.ai/uploads/debug_bundle_deploy_1719760200.zip
Alex Gomez: Got the upload, thanks. Assigning to eng-infra to correlate backend traces. We'll check logs for req_deploy_9c3a and update this thread within 2 business hours. :thumbsup:
